segments.kicker: The Road to the Stock Exchange · Part 4
segments.title: Life after listing
segments.say: Listing day gets the headlines. But the real commitment starts the day after. Here's what life looks like as a listed company in Zimbabwe. This is Reian Creative Finance. Understanding markets. Following capital.

segments.title: Shareholders and their rights
points: Each ordinary share usually carries a vote at general meetings
Shareholders elect directors and approve major decisions
Dividends are paid only when the board declares them, out of profits
No dividend is guaranteed
segments.note: General principles; exact rights are set by the company's constitution and the Companies Act.
segments.say: First, you have new owners. Ordinary shares usually carry votes at general meetings, where shareholders elect directors and approve major decisions. Dividends are paid only when the board declares them out of profits. Nothing is guaranteed.

segments.title: Deadlines that never stop

events.text: Interim results within 3 months of the end of the first six months
Audited annual financial statements published within 3 months
Annual report distributed to shareholders, at least 21 days before the AGM

segments.note: Sources: ZSE SI 134/2019 ss.35, 36, 39; VFEX SI 62/2026 rr.37, 40 (same deadlines).
segments.say: Then the reporting calendar. On both the Z S E and the V F E X, interim results are due within three months of the half year end. Audited annual results must be published within three months of year end, and the annual report sent to shareholders within six months, and at least 21 days before the annual general meeting. And price sensitive news must be disclosed promptly.

segments.title: Share price and market capitalisation
points: Market cap = shares in issue × share price
It changes every trading day
Example: 40 million shares at US$0.50 = US$20m; at US$0.60 = US$24m
A low share price can make future fundraising harder
segments.note: Illustration uses the hypothetical company from Part 3.
segments.say: Now your share price and market capitalisation. Market cap is simply shares in issue times the share price, and it changes every trading day. Our example company from part three has 40 million shares. At 50 cents it's worth 20 million dollars. At 60 cents, 24 million. A weak share price can make it harder to raise money later.

segments.title: Running a listed company properly
steps: A board that challenges management, including independent directors
An AGM every year where shareholders can question the board
segments.note: General good practice expected of listed companies; specific requirements are set by the exchange rules and the Companies Act.
segments.say: Governance matters even more after listing. Investors expect a board that challenges management, including independent directors, audit and remuneration committees, clear rules on conflicts of interest and related party deals, and an annual general meeting where shareholders can question the board face to face. Remember Nvidia from our global markets episode: when governance fails, the share price feels it.

segments.title: What a listing lets you do
points: Rights issues: offer new shares to existing shareholders
Use shares to pay for acquisitions
Employee share ownership schemes
Visibility with lenders, customers and partners
segments.note: General corporate-finance uses; each requires the relevant approvals.
segments.say: A listing also opens doors. A company can do a rights issue, offering new shares to existing shareholders first. It can use its shares to pay for acquisitions, reward staff through employee share schemes, and it gains visibility with lenders and partners.

segments.title: Advantages vs disadvantages

left.head: ADVANTAGES
points: Access to capital
Liquidity for owners
Transparency and credibility
Shares as a currency

right.head: DISADVANTAGES
points: Ongoing compliance costs
Public scrutiny of every result
Loss of some control
Short-term market pressure

segments.note: General comparison. Fee and cost levels vary; the ZSE's 2019 fee schedule may have changed.
segments.say: So it's a trade off. On one side: access to capital, liquidity for owners, credibility and shares you can use as a currency. On the other: ongoing compliance costs, public scrutiny of every result, some loss of control, and pressure from the market every single day.

segments.title: Who is watching
points: The exchange enforces its listing rules
The Securities and Exchange Commission of Zimbabwe (SECZ) oversees the market
The RBZ: foreign holdings and offshore listings (FX Guidelines, Mar 2026)
Breaches can lead to suspension of trading
segments.note: Sources: SI 134/2019; SI 62/2026; RBZ FX Guidelines March 2026 ss.4.2.8, 4.2.18.
segments.say: And you're always being watched. The exchange enforces its rules, the Securities and Exchange Commission oversees the market, and the Reserve Bank's foreign exchange rules cover foreign shareholdings and any listing abroad, which needs its prior approval. Serious breaches can lead to your shares being suspended.

segments.title: Suspension and delisting
points: Suspension: trading halted, often for late results or unclear information
Delisting: the company leaves the exchange
Can be voluntary (e.g. moving to another exchange) or forced
Example: TSL was reported to end its ZSE listing in June 2026 and move to the VFEX
segments.note: Example: The Herald (pre-event report). Process details depend on the exchange's rules.
segments.say: Finally, the exit doors. A suspension halts trading, often because results are late or information is unclear. Delisting means the company leaves the exchange, either voluntarily, for example to move to another exchange, or because it no longer meets the rules. TSL, for example, was reported to end its Z S E listing in June 2026 and move to the V F E X.

segments.title: Listing is a marriage, not a wedding
segments.disclaimer: Educational content only. Not legal or investment advice: speak to a registered legal practitioner and a licensed sponsoring broker before acting. Rules as read on 27 Nov 2026.
segments.say: Listing is a marriage, not a wedding. Prepare for years, report on time every time, and treat your shareholders as partners. That's the end of our road to the stock exchange series. This is educational content, not legal or investment advice. Follow Reian Creative Finance for more.
